cases.reason: Same words, different band. In 2002 the rule itself is headed FORMATS 1, 2, 3, AND 4; in 2023 GR1 is headed FORMAT 1 (catalog band-formats [1]) and reaches formats 2, 3 and 4 only through the separate rows GR11, GR17 and GR21. So the 2023 row alone covers only the format-1 part of the 2002 rule: cause (c), a split the screen missed because 2023 keeps the sentence whole and moves the scope into cross-reference rules. In 2002 the rule also reaches a float item in a communication-section record (cause (a)). The probes show the compiler right at --std 2002 for every reachable part.

cases.reason: Identical rule. The screen section and the screen formats of ACCEPT and DISPLAY are processor-dependent in 2002 (B.3 item 1), and 3.1.5 lets an unclaimed processor-dependent element go unimplemented, with a compile-time warning mechanism. The compiler declines the screen VALUE at --std 2002 with a diagnostic, so the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT verdict carries. (The COBOL1560 text at 2002 cites the 2023 optional-module grounds, not §2002:3.1.5/B.3: a message lead q-09 already raised.)
